shelters.name: Greater Birmingham Humane Society
shelters.description: The oldest and largest animal shelter in Alabama, founded in 1883. GBHS promotes humane treatment of animals through education, advocacy, and services, and manages Animal Care & Control for Jefferson County.

shelters.name: Greater Huntsville Humane Society
shelters.description: A 501(c)(3) no-kill animal shelter rescuing North Alabama's homeless animals for over 55 years. Incorporated in December 1969. Offers community programs including pet food bank and wellness clinic.

shelters.name: Montgomery Humane Society
shelters.description: Founded in 1920, over 100 years of service. Open admission shelter sheltering 10,000+ homeless animals annually. Operates 24/7 rescue, adoption center, and investigates abuse cases.

shelters.name: Mobile SPCA
shelters.description: Founded in 1885 at Temperance Hall in the Port of Mobile, one of Alabama's oldest continuously operating charitable organizations. No-kill, limited intake shelter with adoption guarantee.

shelters.name: Humane Society of West Alabama
shelters.description: Since 1971, a no-kill, volunteer-run, cage-free nonprofit adoption center. Operates entirely on donor support with no government funding or administrative fees.

shelters.name: Morgan County Humane Society
shelters.description: Established in 2004 as the first no-kill organization in North Alabama. Facility sits on over eight acres in rural Morgan County, between Somerville and Hartselle.

shelters.name: Baldwin Humane Society
shelters.description: Founded in 1979, a driving force in animal welfare serving the entire Baldwin County area for over 45 years.

shelters.name: Lee County Humane Society
shelters.description: Developed in 1974, a 501(c)3 non-profit, open-admission shelter serving Auburn and Opelika. Provides adoption services, educational programs, and community awareness.

shelters.name: CARE Humane Society
shelters.description: Offers Auburn and Opelika residents programs and services that strengthen the human-animal bond, prevent cruelty/neglect, provide medical care, and educate on humane treatment.

shelters.name: East Alabama Humane Society
shelters.description: The only no-kill shelter facility within Russell County, Alabama. Best Friends Animal Society partner. Mission is to save lives of as many unwanted pets as possible.

shelters.name: Shelby Humane Society
shelters.description: Founded in 1977 to care for unwanted cats and dogs in Shelby County. Operates the county animal shelter through contract with Shelby County. Offers Shelby Spay Neuter program.

shelters.name: Calhoun County Humane Society
shelters.description: Established in 1973, a 501(c)3 non-profit shelter for homeless pets known as The Animal Shelter, serving Jacksonville, AL and surrounding areas.

shelters.name: Prattville/Autauga Humane Society
shelters.description: A non-profit 501(c)3 animal shelter and adoption center serving the Prattville/Autauga area, providing homeless animals with shelter and care.

shelters.name: Humane Society Pet Rescue and Adoption Center
shelters.description: Saves hundreds of homeless pets in the Gadsden and Attalla areas by providing temporary shelter, food, veterinary care, and educational outreach programs.

shelters.name: Humane Society of Elmore County
shelters.description: Non-profit 501(c)(3) operational for over thirty years. Rescues animals, prevents cruelty, promotes responsible pet ownership, and finds loving homes.

shelters.name: Wiregrass Pet Rescue and Adoption Center
shelters.description: A 501(c)3 nonprofit dedicated to creating an exemplary animal shelter and community-friendly facility in Dothan/Houston County.

shelters.name: Rocket City Rescue
shelters.description: Saves homeless, abused and abandoned animals and gives them a second chance, working to create a no-kill community. Volunteer-driven offering adoption and foster programs.

shelters.name: Crossing Paths Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Established 2006. 501(c)(3) in Blount County dedicated to placing abused, abandoned, and neglected dogs into forever homes. Rescued 1,000+ dogs in 2021. PetSmart Charities $25k grant recipient.

shelters.name: Troy Animal Rescue Project
shelters.description: Federally recognized 501(c)3 non-profit, no-kill rescue serving Alabama and surrounding southern states. Rescues dogs, cats, rabbits, guinea pigs, ferrets, birds, and reptiles.

shelters.name: Island of Misfits
shelters.description: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) dedicated to rescue, rehabilitation, and rehoming of animals in and around Baldwin County, Alabama. Top-rated Alabama rescue.

shelters.name: Paws of Dixie Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Non-profit rescue saving unwanted, abandoned, and neglected animals. Educates community on the significance of spaying and neutering.

shelters.name: H.A.S.R.A. - Heart of Alabama Save Rescue Adopt
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) non-profit, no-kill rescue working with the community, taking in dogs that would otherwise end up at animal control facilities or left homeless.

shelters.name: Full Circle Rescue and Sanctuary
shelters.description: 501(c)(3), 100% volunteer-run, foster-based rescue and sanctuary in central Alabama. Mission to prevent cruelty through rescue, rehabilitation, and adoption.

shelters.name: Wags and Whiskers Mobile
shelters.description: 501(c)3 foster-based animal rescue along the Gulf Coast. No brick and mortar facility - all adoptable animals in foster homes.

shelters.name: Metro Animal Shelter
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) non-profit opened July 1994, funded by City of Tuscaloosa, City of Northport, and Tuscaloosa County Commission.

shelters.name: The Haven No-Kill Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Baldwin County's longest-serving no-kill shelter with 95-99% save rate. Over 700 animals annually receive safety, medical treatment, and second chances.

shelters.name: Safe Harbor Animal Coalition
shelters.description: Helps TNVR cats in South Baldwin County. Surgery Center is private non-profit, high-volume spay/neuter clinic providing low-cost services.

shelters.name: City of Mobile Animal Shelter
shelters.description: City of Mobile municipal animal services. Approximately 1,500 animals brought in annually.

shelters.name: Mobile County Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Mobile County Animal Department working in partnership with community for safe, healthy, caring environment for citizens and animals.

shelters.name: Friends of the Mobile Animal Shelter (FOMAS)
shelters.description: Improves quality of life for shelter pets at City of Mobile Animal Shelter. Finds forever homes for adoptable pets and reduces unwanted pets through spay/neuter programs.

shelters.name: Florence Lauderdale Animal Services
shelters.description: Receives all stray, abandoned, and surrendered pets in Florence and Lauderdale County. Works with fosters, volunteers, and rescues to rehome thousands annually.

shelters.name: Shoals PAWS
shelters.description: All-volunteer group serving Lauderdale, Colbert, and Franklin Counties since 2003. Dedicated to spay/neuter initiatives, TNR, and rescuing animals through foster homes.

shelters.name: CAAWA - Cullman Area Animal Welfare Association
shelters.description: 501(c)3 non-profit, all-volunteer, no-kill organization rescuing dogs and cats in Cullman County to decrease shelter surrenders.

shelters.name: Decatur Animal Services
shelters.description: City of Decatur municipal animal services providing animal control, shelter, and adoption services for the Decatur community.

shelters.name: Huntsville Animal Services
shelters.description: City of Huntsville municipal animal services providing animal control and shelter services for the Huntsville community.

shelters.name: Baldwin County Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Baldwin County government-operated animal shelter providing animal control and adoption services for Baldwin County residents.

shelters.name: Lee County Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Open-admissions and low-kill shelter with a Live Release Rate of over 90%.

shelters.name: Athens Limestone Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Shelters unwanted animals from Limestone County delivered by animal control officers and residents.

shelters.name: Two By Two Rescue League
shelters.description: Faith-based, no-kill rescue saving animal lives for more than 20 years. Mr. Grumplestein's Legacy program provides comprehensive medical care for senior dogs. Grey Muzzle partner.

shelters.name: Luna Farms Rescue
shelters.description: Foster-based rescue committed to reducing overpopulation through adoptions, transports, and spay/neuter programs. Partners with rural shelters to save at-risk senior dogs.

shelters.name: A New Leash on Life
shelters.description: Saves dogs from high-kill shelters and takes in stray or homeless pets, focusing on rural Alabama shelters. Foster-based organization.

shelters.name: Another Chance Dog Rescue
shelters.description: Founded in 2015, spent 10 years improving animal welfare through foster volunteers, transport volunteers, donations, and adoptions.

shelters.name: Animal Rescue Foundation (Mobile)
shelters.description: Nonprofit rescuing homeless or abandoned dogs and cats from overcrowded shelters. Dogs kept in loving foster homes until adopted.

shelters.name: Last Chance Dog Rescue Alabama
shelters.description: All-volunteer foster home based rescue in central Alabama. Rescues strays, abandoned litters, has TNR program, and pulls from rural shelters.

shelters.name: All The Dogs
shelters.description: Animal welfare agency in Shelby County rescuing priority dogs at risk of euthanasia from overcrowded shelters. Foster families help animals decompress and heal.

shelters.name: Big Dog Ranch Rescue - Alabama
shelters.description: Nation's largest cage-free no-kill dog rescue. New 100-acre no cage, no kill facility in Macon County, Alabama.

shelters.name: PAWS of Alabama
shelters.description: Non-profit, no-kill, foster-based rescue without physical shelter. Relies on approved fosters to care for animals until they find forever family.

shelters.name: River Haven Rescue
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to rescue, rehabilitation, foster, and adoption of homeless strays while educating the community in the River Region.

shelters.name: Shoals Animal Advocates
shelters.description: 501(c)3 non-profit foster-based rescue promoting the rescuing, fostering and adoption of homeless dogs and cats in Colbert, Lauderdale, and Franklin counties.

shelters.name: For Paws Rescue
shelters.description: Animal welfare organization in Auburn founded in 2004, dedicated to rescuing and rehoming animals in the Lee County area.

shelters.name: 4Legs4Justice Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Partners with Greater Birmingham Humane Society, operating at a facility in McClellan, Anniston to rescue and rehome animals.

shelters.name: SAVE-A-PET at the Dothan Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Partnership between City of Dothan's Animal Shelter and SAVE A PET non-profit rescue, working to minimize euthanasia of adoptable pets.

shelters.name: Rescue Rangers
shelters.description: Rescue organization in the Decatur area focused on saving and rehoming dogs in North Alabama.

shelters.name: Kitty Kat Haven & Rescue
shelters.description: Registered 501(c)(3) non-profit whose mission is rescue, rehabilitation and adoption of cats of all ages. Increasingly involved in TNR since 2022.

shelters.name: Steel City Cat Rescue
shelters.description: Cat-focused rescue organization in the Birmingham area dedicated to rescuing and rehoming homeless cats.

shelters.name: Azalea City Cat Coalition
shelters.description: Passionate volunteer team serving Baldwin and Mobile Counties. Proactive TNR approach to humanely reduce homeless kittens.

shelters.name: PURRfect Partners of Mobile (PPOM)
shelters.description: Non-profit cat and kitten rescue committed to providing a safe space for homeless cats.

shelters.name: God's Feral Felines
shelters.description: TNR group in Marshall County dedicated to managing feral cat populations through trap-neuter-return.

shelters.name: Save Our Strays Birmingham
shelters.description: TNR group in Jefferson County working to manage stray cat populations.

shelters.name: Saving Grace Animal Rescue
shelters.description: TNR group in Jefferson County focused on cat rescue and population management.

shelters.name: Bama Bully Rescue
shelters.description: Bully breed dog rescue serving Alabama. Works with shelters to pull pit bull type dogs and place in foster care. Best Friends Animal Society partner. Educates on spay/neuter.

shelters.name: German Shepherd Rescue of Central Alabama
shelters.description: Private 501(c)(3) non-profit rescuing German Shepherds from shelters and abusive situations. All dogs spayed/neutered, heartworm free, and vaccinated before adoption.

shelters.name: Helping Shepherds of Every Color Rescue
shelters.description: All-volunteer 501(c)3 based in Montgomery taking in German Shepherd dogs of any color and GSD mixes.

shelters.name: Sweet Home Doberman Rescue
shelters.description: Only 501(c)3 Doberman rescue organization in Alabama, founded in 2015. Top-rated Alabama rescue on Sniffspot.

shelters.name: K9 ResQ of Alabama
shelters.description: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization based in Birmingham dedicated to dog rescue.

shelters.name: Alabama Siberian Husky Rescue
shelters.description: Siberian Husky rescue organization serving Alabama.

shelters.name: Chihuahua Toy Breed Rescue & Retirement
shelters.description: Chihuahua and toy breed rescue also serving as retirement home for small dogs.

shelters.name: SOS - Save Our Snoopies Beagle Rescue
shelters.description: Alabama Chapter of beagle rescue organization serving Gulf Shores and surrounding areas.

shelters.name: Rockin P Rescue - Boxer Rescue
shelters.description: Boxer rescue organization based in Jacksonville, Alabama.

shelters.name: Small Paws Rescue - Alabama
shelters.description: Small breed rescue organization with Alabama chapter. National organization rescuing small dogs.

shelters.name: Hope4Hearts Animal Rescue
shelters.description: Animal rescue organization serving the Mobile area.

shelters.name: Warrior Dog Rescue
shelters.description: Dog rescue organization serving Alabama.

shelters.name: Alabama Wildlife Center
shelters.address: 100 Terrace Drive, Oak Mountain State Park
shelters.description: Founded 1977 by Anne Miller. Largest and oldest wildlife rehab center in Alabama. 501(c) since 1981. Cared for 50,000+ injured birds and mammals over 45+ years. Treats 2,000 wild bird patients annually.

shelters.name: Alabama Wildlife Rescue (AWR)
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) organization helping sick, injured and orphaned wildlife in North Alabama.

shelters.name: Willow Farms Equine Rescue
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) since 2008. Has helped over 1,000 horses find forever homes. Team of 40+ dedicated volunteers. Mission to give horses second chance at life.

shelters.name: Wiregrass Horse Rescue & Sanctuary
shelters.description: Founded 2013 by Lori Flippo. Rescued or assisted with over 200 livestock rescues in and around Alabama. 100% volunteer operated.

shelters.name: Compassion Ranch
shelters.description: Provides compassionate care for 45+ animals in sanctuary for life - horses, ponies, donkeys, dogs, cats, goat and pig. Home to retired US Army cap horse Hank.

shelters.name: Orr Farm Rescue & Sanctuary
shelters.description: Located outside Waverly, offers 25+ miles of nature trails. Operates solely on donations, sponsorship, fundraising events, and trail use passes.

shelters.name: Shorty's Safe Haven
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) non-profit bringing rescue horses and at-risk, struggling girls ages 10-18 together through transformative experience of working with horses and farm animals.

shelters.name: Kindred Hope Rescue and Sanctuary
shelters.description: Founded 2020. Equine assisted therapy program for Veterans, First Responders and community members suffering from anxiety/PTSD.

shelters.name: Calico Junction New Beginnings Ranch
shelters.description: Licensed non-profit rescuing unwanted and abused horses, mules and donkeys across middle Tennessee, Alabama and Kentucky.

shelters.name: Alabama Spay/Neuter Clinic
shelters.description: 501(c)3 nonprofit spay/neuter clinic for cats and dogs dedicated to reducing pet overpopulation and eliminating euthanasia of healthy pets. Feral Cat Program $65.

shelters.name: Alabama Animal Alliance Spay/Neuter Clinic
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) nonprofit providing affordable, high quality, high volume spay/neuter. Open to everyone. Grant funds for Medicaid/Food Stamps recipients. 40+ years combined veterinary experience.

shelters.name: North Alabama Spay Neuter Clinic
shelters.description: Non-profit 501(c) clinic. Mission to end overpopulation of companion animals by providing high quality care to community, rescues and shelters.

shelters.name: Shelby Spay Neuter
shelters.description: Operated by Shelby Humane. Provides low-cost spay/neuter options to pet owners in Central Alabama. Sometimes offers FREE services through grants.

shelters.name: Alabama SPCA
shelters.description: Statewide SPCA organization dedicated to animal welfare across Alabama through rescue, adoption, and advocacy programs.

shelters.name: Bullock County Humane Society
shelters.description: Serves Montgomery area. Focuses on rehabilitation, care, and adoption support for animals in need.

shelters.name: Talladega City Animal Control
shelters.description: City of Talladega animal control services.

shelters.name: Clay County Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Animal shelter serving Clay County, Alabama.

shelters.name: Alabama Veterinary Medical Foundation Spay/Neuter Program
shelters.description: Over 75 veterinarians participate. Net proceeds of Alabama's license plates distributed to help low-income residents spay/neuter their pets.

shelters.name: United Spay Alliance - Alabama
shelters.description: Provides community cats grants and resources for Alabama TNR programs.

notes: Exhaustive collection of Alabama animal shelters, humane societies, rescue organizations, wildlife rehabilitators, farm sanctuaries, and spay/neuter clinics. Greater Birmingham Humane Society (founded 1883) is the oldest and largest shelter in Alabama. Mobile SPCA (founded 1885) is one of the oldest continuously operating charitable organizations. Montgomery Humane Society (founded 1920) has over 100 years of service. Alabama Wildlife Center has cared for 50,000+ injured birds and mammals since 1977. Coverage spans all major cities (Birmingham, Huntsville, Montgomery, Mobile, Tuscaloosa, Dothan, Auburn) and rural areas.
